podcast.title: Formation During Blink 182 Hiatus (Post-2005)
podcast.body: This band was formed by Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker during Blink 182's indefinite hiatus, a period when Mark Hoppus and Tom DeLonge were not speaking. It was one of several solo/side projects that emerged during that time. "Bands like Tom's Angels and Airwaves and Mark and Travis's Plus 44."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Electronic Sound Ambition
podcast.body: The original artistic vision for Plus 44 was to explore a more electronic sound. However, after a period of trial and error in recording, the band's sonic direction evolved into something different from this initial concept. "The original idea was for Plus 44 to be more electronic in its approach, but after a series of false starts and a lot of recording and secrecy, a different sound emerged."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

podcast.title: Formation and Origin of Name
podcast.body: Plus 44 was formed by Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker during Blink-182's hiatus, initially conceived as a more electronic project. The band's name, "Plus 44," was inspired by the international dialing code for the United Kingdom, where the idea for the band first germinated among its members. "Mark Hoppiss and Travis Barker formed a band that they called Plus 44. That name comes from the code you have to use to call the UK."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

podcast.title: Formation by Mark and Travis (Post-Blink 182)
podcast.body: Mark and Travis formed this new band after Blink 182 split, and it "did okay." "Well, Mark and Travis stuck together in a new band they called Plus 44, which also did okay."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Reunions: Some Lasted....and Sadly, Some Didn't ｜ Part 1

podcast.title: Plus 44 Tour Experience
podcast.body: The tour supporting the album "When Your Heart Stop's Beating" was a highlight for Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker (members of Plus 44), providing them the opportunity to play small clubs again after a long time, which was a re-energizing experience. During this tour, Travis Barker broke his arm during a video shoot, causing him immense pain and forcing him to miss several gigs. "The best part about it was the tour where Mark and Tom got to play small clubs for the first time in a long time. That was really energizing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Formation and Personal Struggles
xref.body: Angels & Airwaves was formed by Tom DeLonge during Blink-182's hiatus. This period was marked by personal struggles for Tom, including a nervous breakdown attributed to the Blink-182 breakup, a severe back condition, and addiction to painkillers, which affected his clarity of thought. He dedicated months to working on new material in his home studio, teaching himself piano and audio engineering, finding the process therapeutic. "Tom was completely invisible the entire time, Plus 44 was in the news. The breakup of Blink caused what he'd later call a nervous breakdown."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 3

xref.title: Jerry Finn's Push for Other Projects
xref.body: Longtime producer Jerry Finn, along with Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker, made it clear they wanted to work on another project during Blink-182's hiatus. This desire led to the formation of Plus 44 by Mark and Travis, further solidifying the band's fragmentation. "It also didn't help the situation that the other two thirds of the band and their long time producer Jerry Finn made it very clear that they wanted to work together on another project."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
